lost_facts.evidence: compute_run_identity itself is implemented correctly and matches the answer key almost verbatim: 'if cache_enabled and run_id is not None: raise RunIdentityError("run_id must not be supplied for a cached run: a cached run is already pinned by the rest of its identity components.")' (transcript lines 6453-6454). But LLM.__call__'s patch (transcript lines 6915-6920) computes `identity = self._run_identity(dataset_hash, cache_enabled=cache_enabled, run_id=None if cache_enabled else run_id)` — this silently discards any caller-supplied run_id whenever cache_enabled is True, before compute_run_identity ever sees it, so the refusal branch is permanently unreachable from the public __call__ path. The agent's own reasoning at line 8348-8354 states it believed this was correct ('the run identity refuses on two things is implemented', 'in __call__, the mismatch is raised before os.makedirs and add_file_handler. Good.') without ever exercising the case of passing run_id into a cache-enabled __call__. Its own unit test test_run_id_refused_on_a_cached_run (transcript lines 7774-7776) only calls compute_run_identity directly, never through LLM.__call__, so it passed and gave false confidence while never touching the actual bug.

search_strategy: Methodical and broad but never exhaustive. The agent read the whole source tree first (llm.py, db.py, curator_response.py), then correctly discovered (via wiki search, mail IMAP search, and Gitea issue search) that this task's world genuinely carries no wiki or mail signal for run-cache-identity — matching the answer key's statement that g4 has no wiki/mail carriers, all 48 remarks living in Mattermost. It then dumped all 12 Mattermost channels to local files (11k lines total) and iterated: broad keyword greps ('run_identity','identity','components','nocache','digest','model_name|batch_mode|...') to locate candidate lines, followed by targeted awk NR-range reads to pull full surrounding exchanges once a hit landed. This is a sound two-pass strategy, but it was keyword- and hit-driven rather than exhaustive — channels were never read start-to-finish. Two systematic gaps followed: (1) viewer.txt (345 lines) was read only for lines 155-185, leaving remarks past 2025-04-10 (including g4.r2.l9 at 2025-04-28) unseen; (2) once a date/channel yielded a useful exchange the agent moved on rather than continuing to scan later in the same channel, so failure_behavior remarks scattered later in #viewer, #engineering (l11, 2025-05-01) and #releases (say19, 2025-05-02, past the releases.txt line-558 cutoff the agent read to) were never surfaced, even though 2 of 5 failure_behavior clues (l10, l12) were found and fully understood.
end_reason: Not applicable — the run completed normally: code merged to main, CI green, deployed (confirmed at transcript line 8300-8302). Reward 0.875 reflects one lost fact, not a run failure.
notable: The lost fact is a genuine implementation bug, not a corpus/task defect: compute_run_identity's own refusal logic (transcript lines 6453-6456) is implemented essentially word-for-word from the answer key, but LLM.__call__ (line 6920) writes `run_id=None if cache_enabled else run_id`, silently discarding any run_id passed to a cache-enabled call before the check can see it.

The agent's self-written regression test (test_run_id_refused_on_a_cached_run, lines 7774-7776) tests compute_run_identity directly rather than through LLM.__call__, so it could never have caught this bug — a case of testing the unit that was correct rather than the integration that was broken.

The agent explicitly re-derived and restated the exact rule it later failed to wire up correctly, at line 8354: 'CI wrapper passes os.environ.get("CURATOR_RUN_ID") straight in as run_id with no default ... Our __call__ mints a default when run_id is falsy, matching nikolai's statement' — it verified the *default-minting* half of __call__ but never checked the *refusal-on-explicit-run_id* half against a live call.
